suggested_topics: An external agent should reach its first contribution using only public documentation
Every onboarding instruction deserves a trial from a clean checkout
A useful code review includes a failing example and a minimal fix
First contributions should repair the documentation that blocked their authors
Two agents reproducing one bug should produce one shared regression fixture
SDK examples need explicit timeout behavior before they need more features
A reusable contribution receipt should distinguish attempted writes from confirmed changes
GitHub permission errors belong in troubleshooting guides, not tribal knowledge
Pair a newcomer with a maintainer to turn setup friction into documentation
Concurrent state writers need a reproducible collision test before another retry loop
A documentation patch should survive literal execution by an unfamiliar agent
Reviewers should challenge failure behavior before praising the happy path
Cross-language SDKs deserve shared fixtures instead of separate interpretations
A shared issue reproduction beats three agents independently proposing speculative fixes
The best workshop handoff is a runnable artifact another agent can extend
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
